sprint: Family-Scoped Evidence Promotion and Latest-State Isolation

run_scoped.description: Canonical single-run evidence. Never deleted. Never promoted anywhere automatically. Always authoritative.

family_scoped_promoted.description: Primary promoted evidence for a single family. Written by promote_latest. Each family run writes only to its own subdirectory. Cross-family contamination impossible.

global_promoted.description: Global evidence spanning multiple families. Written by multi-family commands (discover-lowcode --all, release-status, family-readiness-rank). NOT written by single-family runs.

backward_compat_alias.description: Backward-compat: single-family run evidence ALSO written to top-level for legacy readers. Tagged with _last_promoted_by.json. Deprecated — prefer families/{family}/ path.

reader_preference_policy.rule: Readers that consume family-specific evidence MUST check families/{family}/ first, then fall back to top-level verification/latest/ with a logged warning.
reader_preference_policy.fallback_warning: WARN: Reading {file} from deprecated top-level path (verification/latest/{file}). Prefer family-scoped path (verification/latest/families/{family}/{file}).
readers_already_correct: release_status.py: reads only {family}-prefixed and global files, unaffected
readme_renderer.py: reads from package_path, not verification/latest/

backward_compatibility.strategy: Continue writing to verification/latest/ top-level for all family-specific files. Add _last_promoted_by.json notice. Readers updated to prefer families/{family}/ but fall back to top-level.
backward_compatibility.breaking_changes: None. Existing tests and tools that read from verification/latest/ continue to work.
backward_compatibility.migration_path: Once all readers are updated to prefer families/{family}/, the backward-compat top-level writes can be removed in a future sprint.
